- Generates the positive endocochlear potential.
- Provides metabolic support to the scala media.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
coreConcept: Types of Deafness: Sensorineural Hearing Loss
front: A patient experiences sudden hearing loss after using high-dose aminoglycoside antibiotics. Tests show loss of both air and bone conduction. Identify the type of deafness and the likely site of pathology.
back:
- Nerve (Sensorineural) Deafness.
- Site: Damage to Organ of Corti (hair cells) or cochlear nerve.
- Characteristic: Loss of bone conduction (unlike conduction deafness).

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: How does the cochlea discriminate sound frequencies between 20 Hz and 200 Hz where the Place Principle is less effective?
back:
- Volley (Frequency) Principle.
- Nerve impulses synchronize to the specific sound frequency.
- Low-frequency signals are decoded by cochlear nuclei based on volley rate.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
coreConcept: Inner Ear Fluids: Endolymph vs. Perilymph
front: Contrast the biochemical composition and anatomical location of endolymph versus perilymph within the cochlea.
back:
- Endolymph: High K+, low Na+; found in scala media.
- Perilymph: High Na+, low K+ (similar to CSF); found in scala vestibuli and scala tympani.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Identify the small opening at the tip of the cochlea where the scala vestibuli and scala tympani communicate.
back:
- Helicotrema.
- Allows fluid pressure waves to travel between the two chambers.
- Located at the cochlear apex.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: The [___] membrane is so thin and easily moved that it does not obstruct sound vibrations, effectively allowing the scala vestibuli and scala media to function as a single chamber for fluid conduction.
back:
Reissner’s Membrane (Vestibular Membrane)
• Separates scala vestibuli from scala media.
• Maintains the unique ionic environment of the endolymph.
• Transmits pressure waves from perilymph to the cochlear duct.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: A 55-year-old patient with chronic exposure to industrial noise shows a loss of high-frequency hearing. This damage typically begins at the [___] of the cochlea, where the basilar membrane is most sensitive to high pitches.
back:
Base of the Cochlea
• Contains short, stiff basilar fibers.
• Resonates specifically with high-frequency sound waves.
• Chronic loud noise primarily exhausts these proximal hair cells.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Explain the role of the 'Stria Vascularis' in maintaining the electrical environment of the inner ear.
back:
Endocochlear Potential Generation:
• Highly vascular area on the outer wall of scala media.
• Secretes Potassium (K+) into endolymph.
• Maintains a +80mV positive potential relative to perilymph, sensitizing hair cells.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
coreConcept: Inner vs. Outer Hair Cell Dynamics
front: Contrast the functional roles of 'Inner Hair Cells' versus 'Outer Hair Cells' within the Organ of Corti.
back:
Hair Cell Specialization:
• Inner (3,500): Primary transducers; stimulate 90-95% of auditory nerve fibers.
• Outer (12,000): Electromotility function; 'tune' the sensitivity and frequency discrimination of inner hair cells.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Describe the mechanical transduction process that occurs when stereocilia bend toward the longest hair in a bundle.
back:
Mechanoelectrical Transduction:
• Tip links tug open cation channels.
• Potassium (K+) influx from endolymph occurs.
• Depolarization opens voltage-gated Calcium channels, triggering excitatory neurotransmitter release.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: The scala vestibuli and scala tympani communicate at the apex of the cochlea through a small opening called the [___].
back:
Helicotrema
• Located at the cochlear tip.
• Site of continuity between the two perilymph-filled chambers.
• Allows pressure equilibration for extremely low-frequency sounds.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: A patient presents with 'Nerve Deafness.' Following the physiological pathway, identify the collection of neuronal cell bodies that form the auditory nerve within the modiolus.
back:
Spiral Gallion of Corti
• Bipolar neurons residing in the modiolus.
• Axons (approx. 30,000) form the cochlear nerve.
• Transmits signals from hair cells to the medulla.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Identify the structural unit of the Organ of Corti that provides a rigid support for hair cells, ensuring they move as a single unit with the basilar membrane.
back:
Reticular Lamina & Rods of Corti
• Forms a stiff plate supporting the apical ends of hair cells.
• Anchored to basilar fibers.
• Facilitates the 'shearing' motion against the tectorial membrane.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Distinguish between 'Perilymph' and 'Endolymph' regarding their location and chemical composition.
back:
Cochlear Fluids:
• Perilymph: In scala vestibuli/tympani; high Sodium (Na+), resembles CSF.
• Endolymph: In scala media; high Potassium (K+), resembles intracellular fluid; crucial for depolarization.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: What is the 'Place Principle' of frequency determination in the cochlea?
back:
Spatial Coding:
• Different sound frequencies cause maximal vibration at specific points.
• High frequencies peak at the base; low frequencies peak at the apex.
• Stimulates specific nerve fibers corresponding to those locations.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Short, stiff fibers of the basilar membrane located near the oval window resonate best with [___] sound frequencies.
back:
High-frequency sounds.
- Fibers at the base are short, stiff, and elastic.
- Stiffness decreases 100-fold toward the apex (helicotrema).
- This physical gradient allows for spatial frequency discrimination.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: A 75-year-old patient reports difficulty hearing high-pitched doorbells but can hear low-frequency drums clearly. Degradation of hair cells in which specific anatomical region of the cochlea explains this?
back:
The base of the cochlea.
- High-frequency vibrations occur maximally near the oval window.
- Age-related hearing loss (presbycusis) typically destroys basal hair cells first.
- Low frequencies are preserved as they stimulate the apex.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Explain the role of the stria vascularis in maintaining the endocochlear potential within the scala media.
back:
- Secretes endolymph rich in potassium (K+).
- Maintains a +80 mV potential relative to perilymph.
- Creates a +150 mV gradient across hair cell membranes.
- High voltage sensitizes the hair cells to minimal sound stimuli.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Contrast the primary physiological roles of inner hair cells versus outer hair cells in the Organ of Corti.
back:
- Inner Hair Cells: Primary sensory receptors (90-95% of auditory nerve fibers).
- Outer Hair Cells: Act as mechanical amplifiers; they "tune" sensitivity by changing length/stiffness.
- Damage to outer cells causes severe hearing threshold elevation.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Outline the steps of mechanical transduction that occur when stereocilia are bent toward the tallest cilium (kinocilium).
back:
- Tip links pull open cation channels.
- K+ from endolymph flows into the hair cell, causing depolarization.
- Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open, triggering glutamate release.
- Reverse bending causes channel closure and hyperpolarization.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: The fluid filling the scala media, which is unique for its high potassium and low sodium concentration, is called [___].
back:
Endolymph.
- Secreted by the stria vascularis.
- Bathes the stereocilia (apical surface) of hair cells.
- Chemically distinct from the perilymph found in other cochlear chambers.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: A patient treated with high-dose Gentamicin for sepsis develops sudden-onset sensorineural deafness. Which inner ear structures are the primary target of this ototoxicity?
back:
Organ of Corti (Hair cells).
- Aminoglycosides are selectively toxic to sensory hair cells.
- Results in permanent nerve deafness.
- Often affects high-frequency basal hair cells before apical ones.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: How does the "Place Principle" facilitate the discrimination of sound frequency within the inner ear?
back:
- Assigns specific frequencies to discrete locations along the basilar membrane.
- Base (stiff/short) = High frequency.
- Apex (limber/long) = Low frequency.
- Auditory nerve fibers maintain this spatial map to the brainstem.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Distinguish between the anatomical location and communication of perilymph versus endolymph.
back:
- Perilymph: In scala vestibuli/tympani; communicates with subarachnoid space/CSF.
- Endolymph: Confined to scala media; high K+ concentration.
- The Reissner’s and basilar membranes act as barriers between the two.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Identify the anatomical feature at the apex of the cochlea where the scala vestibuli and scala tympani meet.
back:
The Helicotrema.
- Allows fluid pressure waves to pass between perilymph chambers.
- Located at the terminal tip of the cochlear coil.
- Resonates with the lowest audible sound frequencies.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
coreConcept: Functional Anatomy of the Basilar Membrane
front: The inner ear contains a fibrous structure called the [___] membrane, which houses 20,000 to 30,000 stiff, elastic fibers that increase in length from the base to the apex.
back: Basilar membrane

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: A 70-year-old male shows significant hearing loss at high frequencies on an audiogram, with both air and bone conduction equally depressed. Identify the likely site of anatomical damage.
back: Base of the Cochlea

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Explain the role of the stria vascularis in generating the endocochlear potential.
back:
- Actively secretes potassium (K+) into scala media
- Generates +80 mV potential relative to perilymph
- High potential sensitizes hair cell stereocilia
- Essential for mechanical-to-electrical transduction

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
coreConcept: Internal vs. External Hair Cell Physiology
front: Contrast the anatomical arrangement and functional priority of the inner hair cells versus the outer hair cells within the Organ of Corti.
back:
- Inner: Single row (3,500 cells); stimulates 95% of auditory nerve fibers
- Outer: 3-4 rows (12,000 cells); primarily "tunes" pitch sensitivity
- Inner cells: Primary sensory transducers
- Outer cells: Electromotility function

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Specify the role of the 'Place Principle' in the nervous system's determination of sound frequency.
back:
- Spatial mapping of frequency on basilar membrane
- High frequencies: Resonate at the base (oval window)
- Low frequencies: Resonate at the apex (helicotrema)
- CNS identifies pitch based on which nerve fibers fire

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: The scala media is filled with [___], a fluid characterized by high potassium and low sodium concentrations, secreted by the stria vascularis.
back: Endolymph

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: During an inner ear examination, a patient is found to have a lesion at the helicotrema. Which specific range of sound frequencies would be most affected by this defect?
back: Low-frequency sounds

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Describe the mechanical mechanism by which movement of the basilar membrane leads to hair cell depolarization.
back:
- Basilar membrane vibration moves the reticular lamina
- Causes stereocilia to shear against the tectorial membrane
- Tip-links pull open potassium channels
- Influx of K+ triggers glutamate release

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Distinguish between the perilymph of the scala vestibuli and the endolymph of the scala media regarding their anatomical source and ionic nature.
back:
- Perilymph: Similar to CSF; communicates with subarachnoid space
- Endolymph: High K+, low Na+; secreted by stria vascularis
- Potential: Endolymph is +80mV relative to perilymph

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
coreConcept: Anatomy of the Organ of Corti
front: Identify the rigid unit composed of rods that supports the hair cells and moves as a single structure during sound vibration.
back: Reticular Lamina

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: The attenuation reflex is primarily mediated by the contraction of two middle ear muscles: the [___] and the tensor tympani.
back:
* Stapedius muscle
* Pulls the stapes outward away from the oval window
* Opposes the tensor tympani's inward pull
* Increases ossicular rigidity to dampen sound transmission.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: A factory worker notices he can hear his colleague's voice more clearly despite heavy low-frequency machinery noise. Which physiological mechanism facilitates this?
back:
* The Attenuation Reflex
* Selectively masks low-frequency background noise (<1000 Hz)
* Enhances the signal-to-noise ratio for higher-frequency speech
* Increases the overall rigidity of the ossicular chain.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: Explain the specific mechanical role of the Stapedius muscle upon activation of the tympanic reflex.
back:
* Pulls the stapes outward at the oval window
* Increases the tension and rigidity of the ossicular lever system
* Specifically attenuates low-frequency sound conduction (below 1000 cycles/sec)
* Protects the cochlea from damaging vibrations.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: Contrast the vector of force exerted by the tensor tympani versus the stapedius muscle during loud sound exposure.
back:
* Tensor tympani: Pulls the handle of the malleus inward
* Stapedius: Pulls the stapes outward
* Result: Opposing forces increase ossicular stiffness
* Benefit: Reduces sound intensity by 30-40 decibels.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: List the three primary functional significances of the attenuation reflex in human physiology.
back:
* Protection: Prevents cochlear damage from loud sounds
* Masking: Filters out low-frequency background noise
* Speech Regulation: Dampens the speaker's own voice via collateral nerve signals.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: The attenuation reflex can reduce the intensity of low-frequency sound conduction into the cochlea by approximately [___] decibels.
back:
* 30 to 40 decibels
* Equivalent to the difference between a loud voice and a whisper
* Maximum effect occurs on frequencies below 1000 Hz.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: A patient experiences extreme auditory discomfort while speaking their own name, yet their external hearing threshold is normal. A defect in which reflex is likely?
back:
* Attenuation reflex (Self-vocalisation dampening)
* The brain normally sends collateral signals to middle ear muscles during speech
* This reduces sensitivity to one's own voice to prevent auditory overloading.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: Why does the attenuation reflex fail to protect the ear against sudden, percussive sounds like a gunshot?
back:
* Reflex Latency: 40 to 80 milliseconds
* Percussive sounds reach the cochlea before the muscles contract
* Damage occurs during the initial wave before the ossicular chain stiffens.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: Distinguish between the effect of the attenuation reflex on sound frequencies above 1000 Hz versus those below 1000 Hz.
back:
* Below 1000 Hz: Significant attenuation (30-40 dB reduction)
* Above 1000 Hz: Minimal effect, preserving important speech information
* Significance: This allows for effective communication in noisy environments.

category: Describe the mechanism of attenuation reflex and its significance
front: Which cranial nerves provide the motor innervation for the two muscles involved in the attenuation reflex?
back:
* CN V (Trigeminal): Innervates the tensor tympani
* CN VII (Facial): Innervates the stapedius
* Both are required for the full dampening effect of the reflex.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The basilar membrane contains fibers that are short and stiff near the [___], where they resonate best with high-frequency sound waves.
back:
• Oval window.
• Stiffness decreases 100-fold toward the apex.
• Short, stiff fibers resonate with high-pitch sounds; long, limber fibers resonate with low-pitch sounds.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A 70-year-old patient struggles to hear high-pitched doorbells but hears low-pitched voices clearly. This deficit indicates damage specifically at the [___] of the cochlea.
back:
• Base of the cochlea.
• High-frequency waves dissipate energy early near the stapes.
• Basal hair cells are most susceptible to aging and ototoxic drugs.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Mechanical Transduction in the Organ of Corti
front: Explain the mechanical process that occurs between the basilar membrane and the tectorial membrane during sound vibration.
back:
• Upward movement of the basilar membrane rocks the reticular lamina inward.
• Stereocilia shear against the stationary tectorial membrane.
• This mechanical bending triggers the opening of cation-conducting channels.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the functional roles of inner hair cells and outer hair cells in auditory transmission.
back:
• Inner Hair Cells: Primary receptors; stimulate 90-95% of auditory nerve fibers.
• Outer Hair Cells: Electromechanical amplifiers; 'tune' the sensitivity of inner hair cells for different pitches.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the source and electrical value of the potential that sensitizes hair cells within the scala media.
back:
• Stria vascularis (secretes K+).
• +80 millivolts (Endocochlear potential).
• Creates a 150 mV gradient between the endolymph and the hair cell interior.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The pressure wave initiated by the stapes at the oval window moves along the basilar membrane toward the [___] at the cochlear apex.
back:
• Helicotrema.
• Termed a 'Traveling Wave'.
• Wave velocity decreases as it progresses toward the wider, more flexible apex.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient's audiogram shows significant hearing loss via air conduction but normal bone conduction. State the most likely anatomical site of impairment.
back:
• Middle ear (Ossicular system/Tympanic membrane).
• Diagnosis: Conduction Deafness.
• Indicates the cochlea and auditory nerve are intact, but sound transmission is blocked.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the specific ionic mechanism triggered when stereocilia are bent toward the longest cilium.
back:
• Tip link filaments pull open cation channels.
• K+ enters from endolymph, causing depolarization.
• Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open, triggers glutamate release onto the spiral ganglion.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish between the 'Place Principle' and the 'Volley Principle' in frequency determination.
back:
• Place Principle: Frequency identified by the specific site of maximal basilar resonance.
• Volley Principle: Low frequencies (20-2000Hz) determined by synchronized nerve impulse firing rates.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain why the outward bulging of the round window is essential for cochlear function.
back:
• Cochlea is encased in unyielding bone.
• Fluid is incompressible.
• Bulging allows the stapes to move inward, enabling pressure wave transmission through the scalae.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: The scala media is filled with [___], a unique extracellular fluid characterized by high potassium and low sodium concentrations, secreted by the stria vascularis.
back: Endolymph. - Essential for the +80 mV endocochlear potential. - Bathes the upper surfaces/stereocilia of hair cells. - High K+ concentration drives depolarization.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: A patient treated with Gentamicin develops high-frequency hearing loss. This drug typically causes sensorineural deafness by damaging the hair cells located at the [___] of the cochlea.
back: Base of the cochlea. - High-frequency resonance occurs near the oval window. - Stiff, short basilar fibers are located here. - Aminoglycosides are specifically ototoxic to these receptors.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Explain the mechanical transduction process that leads to depolarization of hair cells when stereocilia are bent toward the longest cilium.
back: - Tip links pull open mechanical cation channels. - K+ ions flow from endolymph into the hair cell. - Voltage-gated calcium channels open. - Glutamate is released to the spiral ganglion neurons.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
coreConcept: Inner vs Outer Hair Cell Function
front: Contrast the primary physiological roles of inner hair cells versus outer hair cells within the Organ of Corti.
back: - Inner Hair Cells: Primary sensory transducers (90-95% of auditory nerve stimulation). - Outer Hair Cells: 'Cochlear amplifiers' or tuners; adjust sensitivity/pitch via electromechanical shortening and stiffness changes.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: How does the structural variation of the basilar membrane from the oval window to the helicotrema facilitate the 'Place Principle'?
back: - Base: Narrow, stiff fibers vibrate to high frequencies. - Apex: Long, limber fibers vibrate to low frequencies. - Each frequency has a specific 'place' of maximum vibration/resonance.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: The [___] potential, measuring approximately +80 mV, is the highest positive potential in the body and sensitizes hair cells to minimal vibrations.
back: Endocochlear potential. - Maintained by the stria vascularis. - Exists between endolymph and perilymph. - Crucial for the extreme sensitivity of human hearing.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: A 40-year-old female presents with progressive hearing loss; bone conduction is normal, but air conduction is decreased. Identify the most likely inner ear-related anatomical cause.
back: Stapes Ankylosis (Otosclerosis). - Fixation of the stapes faceplate to the oval window. - Disrupts impedance matching between air and cochlear fluid. - Bone conduction bypasses the middle ear ossicles.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Describe the fluid and membrane dynamics in the cochlea that occur simultaneously with the inward movement of the stapes.
back: - Stapes pushes into the oval window. - Pressure wave travels through scala vestibuli. - Basilar membrane bends toward the scala tympani. - Round window bulges outward to relieve fluid pressure.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Differentiate between perilymph and endolymph regarding their anatomical location and ionic similarity to other body fluids.
back: - Perilymph: Located in scala vestibuli/tympani; high Na+/low K+ (similar to CSF). - Endolymph: Located in scala media; high K+/low Na+ (similar to intracellular fluid).

category: Describe the physiological anatomy of inner ear
front: Identify the anatomical structure at the cochlear apex that allows communication between the scala vestibuli and the scala tympani.
back: Helicotrema. - Small opening at the tip of the cochlea. - Site where low-frequency vibrations (below 200 Hz) are typically localized. - Connects the perilymphatic spaces.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Incompressibility and Fluid Displacement in the Cochlea
front: The initial inward movement of the stapes footplate against the oval window is compensated by the outward bulging of the [___].
back:
* Round window (Fenestra rotunda).
* This allows for the displacement of incompressible cochlear fluid.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A 65-year-old patient presents with age-related hearing loss (presbyacusis), primarily affecting high-frequency sounds. Pathologically, the most likely site of initial damage is the [___] of the cochlea.
back:
* Base of the cochlea (near the oval window).
* This region contains short, stiff basilar fibers that resonate at high frequencies.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Mechanoreception in the Organ of Corti
front: Explain the role of the Tectorial Membrane in the generation of hair cell receptor potentials.
back:
* It serves as a rigid overlying structure.
* Upward basilar membrane movement causes shearing of stereocilia against it.
* This shearing force mechanically opens potassium channels in stereocilia.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish between the Place Principle and the Volley Principle in sound frequency discrimination.
back:
* Place Principle: High/Medium frequencies (specific basilar membrane locations).
* Volley Principle: Low frequencies (20-2000 Hz; synchronized nerve impulse firing patterns).

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: How does the Endocochlear Potential contribute to the extreme sensitivity of cochlear hair cells?
back:
* Maintains endolymph at +80 mV (high potassium).
* Creates a steep ~150 mV electrical gradient across the stereocilia tips.
* This allows rapid K+ influx upon minimal mechanical stimulation.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The cochlear fluid that is high in potassium and low in sodium, filling the scala media, is called [___].
back:
* Endolymph.
* It is secreted by the stria vascularis.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient develops deafness after taking high-dose Gentamicin. Pathophysiologically, the primary site of damage within the cochlea is the [___].
back:
* Hair cells (specifically Outer Hair Cells).
* Aminoglycosides are ototoxic and destroy the sensory receptors in the Organ of Corti.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the sequence of the 'Traveling Wave' in the cochlea during sound transmission.
back:
* Starts at the base and moves toward the helicotrema.
* Amplitude increases until it reaches a resonant point.
* Dissipates rapidly after the peak amplitude point.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the physical properties of the basilar fibers at the base versus the apex of the cochlea.
back:
* Base: Short, stiff, narrow fibers (High frequency).
* Apex: Long, limber, wider fibers (Low frequency).

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the primary excitatory neurotransmitter released by the inner hair cells onto the spiral ganglion dendrites.
back:
* Glutamate.
* Released following calcium-mediated exocytosis triggered by cell depolarization.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The basilar membrane contains fibers that increase in length but decrease in [___] as they progress from the base of the cochlea toward the helicotrema.
back:
Stiffness (or Diameter). 
- Base: Short, stiff fibers (High frequency). 
- Apex: Long, limber fibers (Low frequency).

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: An elderly patient with age-related hearing loss (presbycusis) shows significant impairment specifically for high-frequency sounds. Identify the specific region of the cochlea most likely affected.
back:
The Base of the cochlea. 
- High-frequency resonance occurs near the oval window. 
- This area undergoes maximum mechanical stress and hair cell degeneration.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain the role of the +80 mV Endocochlear Potential in the mechanism of hair cell excitation.
back:
Creates a 150 mV driving force. 
- High K+ in endolymph (+80mV) vs. negative hair cell interior (-70mV). 
- Pulls K+ rapidly into stereocilia upon mechanical opening of channels.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Inner vs. Outer Hair Cell Function
front: Contrast the functional roles of Inner Hair Cells (IHCs) versus Outer Hair Cells (OHCs) in auditory signal transduction.
back:
IHCs: Primary receptors; 90-95% of auditory nerve stimulation. 
- OHCs: 'Cochlear amplifiers'; adjust stiffness to 'tune' the sensitivity and frequency discrimination of IHCs.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the two primary mechanical components of the middle ear that facilitate 'Impedance Matching' between air and cochlear fluid.
back:
Area Ratio & Lever System. 
- Area Ratio: TM to Stapes (17:1). 
- Lever System: Malleus to Incus (1.3:1). 
- Total force magnification: ~22 times.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The mechanical opening of cation channels in hair cells is mediated by the tension on thin protein filaments called [___].
back:
Tip links. 
- Connect shorter stereocilia to adjacent longer ones. 
- Tugged outward during bending toward the longer stereocilia, opening K+ channels.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient with a middle ear infection develops stiffening of the ossicular chain. Explain the physiological significance of the resulting hearing loss in terms of sound transmission.
back:
Loss of Impedance Matching. 
- Sound reflects off the oval window rather than entering the fluid. 
- Results in a conduction deafness of 15-20 decibels.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the 'Traveling Wave' mechanism as it relates to the dissipation of sound energy in the cochlea.
back:
Waves move along the basilar membrane. 
- Amplitude peaks at the resonant frequency 'place'. 
- Wave dies out immediately after peak, ensuring specific frequency discrimination.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish the composition and origin of Perilymph from that of Endolymph.
back:
Perilymph: High Na+ (like CSF); fills Scalae Vestibuli/Tympani. 
- Endolymph: High K+; fills Scala Media; secreted by Stria Vascularis.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: List the sequence of ionic events in a hair cell following the inward flow of potassium (K+).
back:
Depolarization -> Ca2+ Influx. 
- Depolarization opens voltage-gated Ca2+ channels. 
- Ca2+ triggers Glutamate release onto auditory nerve endings.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The basal end of the basilar membrane contains short, stiff fibers that resonate most effectively with [___] frequencies.
back:
• High frequencies (e.g., 8,000–20,000 Hz)
• Stiffness decreases 100-fold towards the apex
• High-frequency waves dissipate quickly near the base

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient with selective damage to the stria vascularis presents with profound hearing loss. This pathology primarily disrupts the maintenance of the [___].
back:
• Endocochlear potential (+80 mV)
• Caused by active K+ secretion into the scala media
• Provides the electrical gradient for hair cell depolarization

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain the role of 'Tip Links' in the mechanical transduction of sound waves within the Organ of Corti.
back:
• Connect shorter stereocilia to adjacent longer ones
• Bending towards the longest cilium tugs tip links
• Mechanically opens 200–300 cation channels (K+ influx)

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A researcher observes that low-frequency sounds (20–200 Hz) do not have a discrete 'peak' on the basilar membrane. Contrast the two principles used by the CNS to identify these frequencies.
back:
• Place Principle: Frequency determined by location of maximum vibration (better for high tones)
• Volley Principle: Frequency determined by the synchronized rate of nerve firing (essential for low tones)

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the physiological significance of the hair cell's negative intracellular potential relative to the endolymph.
back:
• Intracellular potential is -70 mV vs perilymph
• Total gradient is -150 mV vs endolymph (+80 mV)
• Sensitizes hair cells to detect extremely weak sounds

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The specific fluid found within the scala media that possesses a unique high-potassium, low-sodium composition is called [___].
back:
• Endolymph
• Chemically similar to intracellular fluid
• Bathes the apical stereocilia of hair cells

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A 70-year-old patient presents with Presbycusis (age-related hearing loss), specifically unable to hear high-pitched doorbells. This is due to degeneration of hair cells at the [___] of the cochlea.
back:
• Base (proximal turn)
• Base fibers are shorter and stiffer
• These fibers are the first to encounter high-energy pressure waves

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain the mechanism and purpose of 'electromotility' performed by the Outer Hair Cells (OHCs).
back:
• OHCs physically shorten/lengthen in response to signals
• Function as a 'Cochlear Amplifier'
• Enhances the sensitivity and frequency-tuning of Inner Hair Cells

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the movement of the Oval Window and Round Window during the compression phase of a sound wave.
back:
• Oval Window: Pushed inward by stapes to create perilymph pressure
• Round Window: Bulges outward into middle ear
• Round window acts as a pressure-relief valve

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the primary neurotransmitter released by the base of hair cells into the spiral ganglion synapses.
back:
• Glutamate
• Released upon depolarization and Ca2+ influx
• Triggers action potentials in the cochlear nerve

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The short, stiff fibers of the basilar membrane located near the [___] of the cochlea vibrate most effectively in response to high-frequency sound waves.
back:
• Base (near the oval window).
• These fibers are short and have high stiffness.
• Stiffness decreases 100-fold toward the apex.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A 70-year-old male presents with bilateral high-frequency hearing loss. Pathophysiologically, this condition primarily involves age-related degeneration of the [___].
back:
• Base of the cochlea.
• Affects hair cells and basilar fibers sensitive to high pitches.
• Known as Presbycusis.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the mechanical-to-electrical transduction mechanism that occurs when stereocilia bend toward the longest cilium.
back:
• Tip links pull open cation-conducting channels.
• K+ ions enter from endolymph, causing depolarization.
• Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open.
• Glutamate is released onto cochlear nerve endings.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the primary functional roles of Inner Hair Cells versus Outer Hair Cells in auditory transmission.
back:
• Inner (3,500): 90-95% of auditory nerve stimulation; primary sensory transducers.
• Outer (12,000): Electromotility; 'tune' sensitivity and frequency discrimination.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the physiological principle used by the nervous system to detect sound frequency based on the specific location of maximal basilar membrane stimulation.
back:
• Place Principle.
• High frequencies stimulate the base.
• Low frequencies stimulate the apex (helicotrema).

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The [___] is the specialized vascular structure in the scala media responsible for maintaining the +80 mV endocochlear potential.
back:
• Stria vascularis.
• Secretes K+ ions into the endolymph.
• Maintains the high positive potential required to sensitize hair cells.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient receiving high-dose Streptomycin therapy develops tinnitus and hearing loss. This drug typically causes 'nerve deafness' by damaging the [___].
back:
• Organ of Corti (specifically Hair Cells).
• Aminoglycosides are notoriously ototoxic.
• Results in permanent sensorineural hearing loss.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain why the 'Traveling Wave' along the basilar membrane dissipates and dies out at a specific point for a given frequency.
back:
• The wave reaches a point with a natural resonant frequency equal to the sound.
• Basilar membrane vibrates with such ease that energy is fully dissipated.
• Wave cannot travel further toward the apex.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish between the electrolyte composition of Perilymph and Endolymph.
back:
• Perilymph: High Na+, Low K+ (similar to CSF); in Scala Vestibuli/Tympani.
• Endolymph: High K+, Low Na+; in Scala Media; maintained by stria vascularis.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: What is the specific mechanical role of the Round Window during the inward movement of the stapes?
back:
• Acts as a pressure relief valve.
• Bulges outward into the middle ear.
• Allows incompressible cochlear fluid to move, enabling the traveling wave.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Inward movement of the stapes faceplate at the oval window causes an initial pressure wave in the [___] of the cochlea.
back:
* Perilymph
* Located within the Scala Vestibuli
* Initiates the 'traveling wave' that moves toward the helicotrema.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient is exposed to a pure high-frequency tone of 8000 Hz. Describe where the maximum amplitude of vibration occurs on the basilar membrane.
back:
* Near the base of the cochlea
* Occurs because basilar fibers are short and stiff
* High-frequency waves dissipate quickly after reaching their resonant point.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Mechanical Transduction in Organ of Corti
front: Explain the role of the 'reticular lamina' and 'rods of Corti' in the depolarization of hair cells during sound transmission.
back:
* Form a rigid unit with basilar fibers
* Rock upward/inward during membrane vibration
* Causes stereocilia to shear against the stationary tectorial membrane.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the ionic composition and electrical potential of the endolymph in the scala media with the perilymph in the scala vestibuli.
back:
* Endolymph: High K+, Low Na+; potential of +80mV
* Perilymph: High Na+, Low K+; potential of 0mV
* Potential gradient sensitizes hair cell response.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the specific point at which a sound wave 'dies' or ceases to travel along the basilar membrane.
back:
* At its natural resonant point
* Occurs when membrane frequency matches sound frequency
* All energy is dissipated through maximal back-and-forth vibration.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Very low-frequency sound waves (below 200 Hz) typically travel the entire length of the basilar membrane to reach the [___].
back:
* Helicotrema
* The minute opening at the cochlear apex
* Allows communication between the Scala Vestibuli and Scala Tympani.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A factory worker presents with hearing loss specifically at 4000 Hz. Damage to which specific part of the cochlear duct is most likely responsible?
back:
* Middle portion of the basilar membrane
* Loss of hair cells at that specific resonant site
* Result of chronic mechanical overstimulation.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the molecular mechanism of 'tip-link' filaments when stereocilia are bent toward the longer cilia.
back:
* Tugging opens 200-300 cation channels
* Allows rapid K+ influx from endolymph
* Causes hair cell depolarization and glutamate release.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish between the primary functions of inner hair cells versus outer hair cells in sound transmission.
back:
* Inner: Transmit 90-95% of auditory nerve signals
* Outer: 'Tune' sensitivity and improve pitch discrimination
* Outer cells adjust stiffness via retrograde signals.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: State the significance of Reissner's membrane in the transmission of sound vibrations within the cochlea.
back:
* Offers minimal obstruction to fluid waves
* Maintains high K+ concentration in Scala Media
* Chemically separates endolymph from perilymph.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The basilar fibers of the cochlea increase in length and decrease in diameter as they progress from the [___] toward the helicotrema.
back:
• Oval window (base of cochlea)
• Fibers at the base are short and stiff for high-frequency resonance
• Fibers at the apex are long and limber for low-frequency resonance

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient treated with high-dose Gentamicin develops bilateral high-frequency hearing loss. This sensorineural deficit is primarily caused by damage to the hair cells located at the [___] of the cochlea.
back:
• Basal end (near oval window)
• This area is naturally tuned for high-frequency resonance
• Aminoglycosides selectively damage the Organ of Corti hair cells in this region

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain the role of the 'Traveling Wave' along the basilar membrane upon stapes vibration.
back:
• Fluid movement at the oval window initiates a wave toward the helicotrema
• The wave reaches peak amplitude at its resonant frequency point
• The wave energy dissipates and 'dies' once this resonant point is reached

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Inner vs. Outer Hair Cell Specialization
front: Contrast the physiological roles of Inner Hair Cells (IHCs) versus Outer Hair Cells (OHCs) in cochlear function.
back:
• IHCs (90-95% of afferents): The primary receptors for sound transduction
• OHCs: Act as 'cochlear amplifiers' to tune and sensitize IHCs
• OHCs receive predominantly inhibitory retrograde signals from the brainstem

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the structure responsible for generating the +80mV endocochlear potential and the specific ion it secretes.
back:
• Stria vascularis (outer wall of scala media)
• Actively secretes Potassium (K+) ions into the endolymph
• Maintains the high electrical gradient necessary for hair cell sensitization

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Mechanical transduction in the cochlea occurs when the bending of stereocilia toward the [___] pulls on tip-link proteins to open cation channels.
back:
• Longest stereocilium (outward from the modiolus)
• Opens 200–300 mechanical cation channels
• Resulting Potassium (K+) influx causes rapid hair cell depolarization

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A 65-year-old patient presents with Presbycusis (age-related hearing loss). This condition is usually characterized by the degeneration of fibers at the base of the cochlea, which impairs the detection of [___].
back:
• High-frequency sounds
• The base has high stiffness and low fluid mass loading
• This leads to the characteristic loss of hearing for high-pitched tones

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the unique ionic basis of hair cell depolarization compared to standard neuronal depolarization.
back:
• Depolarization is driven by Potassium (K+) influx rather than Sodium
• K+ moves from high-concentration endolymph (+80mV) into the hair cell (-70mV)
• This massive 150mV gradient allows extreme sensitivity to weak sounds

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish between Perilymph and Endolymph based on their anatomical location and ionic composition.
back:
• Perilymph: Located in Scala Vestibuli/Tympani; high Na+, low K+ (like CSF)
• Endolymph: Located in Scala Media; high K+, low Na+ (like intracellular fluid)
• Separated by the thin Reissner’s membrane

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: How does the 'Place Principle' assist the brain in frequency discrimination?
back:
• Different sound frequencies activate specific 'places' on the basilar membrane
• High-frequency at the base; Low-frequency at the apex
• Specific nerve fibers are activated based on the physical point of maximum vibration

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Sound waves of low frequency (20–200 Hz) achieve maximum resonance and vibration at the [___] of the cochlea, near the helicotrema.
back:
• Apex (distal end) 
 • Contains long, limber basilar fibers 
 • Lowest stiffness allows for low-frequency resonance.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient with prolonged exposure to industrial noise presents with hearing loss specifically at higher pitches. This indicates pathological damage to the basilar membrane at the [___].
back:
• Base of the cochlea 
 • Located near the oval and round windows 
 • Contains short, stiff fibers tuned to high frequencies.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the initial mechanical displacement of the basilar membrane caused by the inward thrust of the stapes against the oval window.
back:
• Fluid moves forward in scala vestibuli 
 • Basilar membrane bends toward the round window 
 • Elastic tension initiates a traveling wave toward the apex.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the physical properties of basilar fibers at the base versus the apex of the cochlea that allow for frequency discrimination.
back:
• Base: Short, stiff fibers; resonant for high frequencies. 
 • Apex: Long, limber fibers; resonant for low frequencies. 
 • Fiber stiffness decreases 100-fold from base to apex.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain the physiological basis of the 'Place Principle' in the cochlea.
back:
• Different sound frequencies excite specific locations on the basilar membrane. 
 • Brain determines frequency by identifying which nerve fibers are maximally stimulated based on their anatomical origin.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Because the cochlea is encased in a rigid bony wall, the inward movement of the stapes at the oval window is only possible if the [___] bulges outward.
back:
• Round window 
 • Acts as a pressure relief valve 
 • Essential for fluid displacement and basilar membrane vibration.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A research model shows a total loss of the +80mV endocochlear potential. Which specific cochlear structure is responsible for maintaining this potential through potassium secretion?
back:
• Stria Vascularis 
 • Located on the outer wall of the scala media 
 • Generates the +80mV potential between endolymph and perilymph.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Why does a high-frequency sound wave 'die' rapidly after entering the cochlea instead of traveling the full length to the helicotrema?
back:
• Wave reaches its resonant point at the stiff base. 
 • Basilar membrane vibrates with maximum ease at this point. 
 • Wave energy is fully dissipated by this localized vibration.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the ionic composition of perilymph (found in scala vestibuli) with endolymph (found in scala media).
back:
• Perilymph: High Na+, Low K+ (resembles CSF). 
 • Endolymph: High K+, Low Na+ (resembles intracellular fluid). 
 • Difference creates the electrochemical gradient for hair cell excitation.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the change in velocity of a sound wave as it travels from the oval window toward the helicotrema.
back:
• Velocity is fast at the base. 
 • Velocity becomes progressively slower toward the apex. 
 • Caused by the decreasing coefficient of elasticity of the basilar fibers.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
coreConcept: Inner Hair Cells vs. Outer Hair Cells
front: The primary sensory receptors within the organ of Corti responsible for transmitting 90-95% of auditory signals to the cochlear nerve are the [___].
back:
• Inner Hair Cells (IHCs)
• Number: ~3,500
• Function: Major transducers of sound into nerve impulses

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A patient with long-term exposure to loud industrial noise shows selective loss of high-frequency hearing. The mechanotransduction at the organ of Corti is initiated by the influx of [___] ions into the stereocilia.
back:
• Potassium (K+)
• Mechanism: Tip links open cation channels
• Fluid source: Endolymph (high K+ concentration)

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
coreConcept: Mechanical Transduction in Organ of Corti
front: Explain the mechanical sequence that occurs in the organ of Corti when the basilar membrane moves upward during a sound vibration.
back:
• Basilar fiber moves up
• Reticular lamina rocks upward and inward toward modiolus
• Stereocilia shear against tectorial membrane
• Results in depolarization

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Contrast the functional role of Outer Hair Cells (OHCs) with that of Inner Hair Cells (IHCs) regarding auditory sensitivity.
back:
• IHCs: Transmit actual sound signals to brain
• OHCs: Function as "cochlear amplifiers"
• OHCs adjust sensitivity/tuning of IHCs via electromotility

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Justify the physiological importance of the 150 mV electrical potential difference across the tips of the stereocilia.
back:
• Sum of endocochlear (+80mV) and intracellular (-70mV) potentials
• High driving force for rapid K+ influx
• Increases sensitivity to extremely weak sounds

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
coreConcept: Anatomy of the Organ of Corti
front: The rigid shelf supported by the rods of Corti, which serves as a frame to hold the apical ends of the hair cells in place, is the [___].
back:
• Reticular lamina
• Function: Provides structural stability during vibration
• Attachment: Connects to basilar fibers via rods of Corti

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Experimental stimulation of retrograde inhibitory nerve fibers from the superior olivary nucleus to the organ of Corti primarily affects which cell group to reduce sound sensitivity?
back:
• Outer Hair Cells (OHCs)
• Effect: Causes OHC shortening or stiffness changes
• Outcome: Selective inhibition of specific sound pitches

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Outline the role of the Tectorial Membrane during the generation of the receptor potential in hair cells.
back:
• Acts as a stationary gelatinous anchor
• Stereocilia tips are embedded in it
• Relative movement causes shearing of hairs
• Mechanical displacement opens ion channels

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Distinguish between the two types of fluid that bathe the different surfaces of a single hair cell in the organ of Corti.
back:
• Apical surface/Hairs: Endolymph (+80mV, high K+)
• Basal/Lower body: Perilymph (0mV, low K+)
• Essential for creating the electrical gradient

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Identify the specific neurotransmitter released by the base of hair cells into the spiral ganglion synapses upon depolarization.
back:
• Glutamate
• Action: Rapidly acting excitatory neurotransmitter
• Trigger: Influx of Ca2+ through voltage-gated channels

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: The organ of Corti is bathed by a unique fluid called endolymph, which is characterized by an exceptionally high concentration of [___] ions.
back: * Potassium (K+). * Secreted by the stria vascularis. * Essential for maintaining the +80 mV endocochlear potential and driving depolarization.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A patient treated with long-term Gentamicin for a severe infection develops bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. The primary anatomical site of permanent damage in this condition is the [___].
back: * Organ of Corti. * Specifically destroys the hair cell receptors. * Results in permanent nerve deafness due to loss of mechanotransduction capability.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Explain the mechanical process that leads to the opening of cation-conducting channels in the stereocilia of the organ of Corti.
back: * Upward basilar membrane movement rocks the reticular lamina. * Stereocilia shear against the tectorial membrane. * Tip link filaments tug open K+ channels on shorter cilia.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
coreConcept: Inner vs. Outer Hair Cell Function
front: Contrast the functional roles of the Inner Hair Cells and the Outer Hair Cells within the organ of Corti.
back: * Inner Hair Cells: Primary transducers; stimulate 90-95 percent of auditory nerve fibers. * Outer Hair Cells: Electromotility; tune sensitivity and frequency discrimination.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: State the physiological significance of the +80 mV endocochlear potential regarding hair cell sensitivity.
back: * Creates a 150 mV gradient across hair cell tips. * Sensitizes hair cells to respond to minimal sound vibrations. * Drives rapid K+ influx during mechanical stimulation.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: The cell bodies of the first-order sensory neurons that carry auditory signals from the hair cells to the brain stem are located in the [___].
back: * Spiral ganglion of Corti. * Located within the modiolus of the cochlea. * Send axons into the cochlear nerve.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A microscopic study of a mutant mouse shows that the tectorial membrane fails to develop. Predict the primary effect on the transduction process in the organ of Corti.
back: * Loss of shearing force on stereocilia. * Failure of tip-link activation and K+ channel opening. * Severe sensorineural deafness despite intact hair cells.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Describe the function of the reticular lamina in the organ of Corti transduction mechanism.
back: * Rigid support plate for hair cell apical ends. * Moves as a unit with basilar fibers and rods of Corti. * Translates vertical vibration into horizontal shearing.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Distinguish between the fluid surrounding the apical surface versus the basolateral surface of hair cells in the organ of Corti.
back: * Apical: Bathed in Endolymph (High K+, +80 mV). * Basolateral: Bathed in Perilymph (Low K+, 0 mV). * This gradient facilitates rapid depolarization.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Identify the primary excitatory neurotransmitter released by the hair cells into the synaptic cleft of the auditory nerve.
back: * Glutamate. * Released upon depolarization-induced calcium influx. * Stimulates cochlear nerve endings to generate action potentials.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The mechanical gate-opening mechanism in cochlear hair cells involves thin filaments called [___] that connect shorter stereocilia to adjacent longer ones.
back:
* Tip links.
* Mechanically pull open cation channels.
* Triggered by bending toward the longest stereocilia.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A 70-year-old male presents with difficulty hearing high-pitched doorbells and female voices. This condition, presbycusis, is primarily caused by degenerative changes at the [___] of the cochlea.
back:
* Base of the cochlea.
* High-frequency resonance occurs here.
* Fibers are short and stiff.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain the physiological reason why a 'traveling wave' along the basilar membrane dissipates and 'dies' at a specific point.
back:
* Reaches natural resonant frequency.
* Basilar membrane vibrates with maximum amplitude.
* Energy is fully dissipated at that specific locus.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Contrast the physical characteristics of the basilar membrane fibers at the base of the cochlea versus those at the apex (helicotrema).
back:
* Base: Short, stiff fibers (High frequency resonance).
* Apex: Long, limber fibers (Low frequency resonance).
* Stiffness decreases 100-fold from base to apex.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Inner vs Outer Hair Cell Function
front: Identify the specific cells in the Organ of Corti that, despite being fewer in number, stimulate approximately 90% to 95% of the auditory nerve fibers.
back:
* Inner hair cells.
* Primary transducers of sound.
* Synapse directly with spiral ganglion neurons.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The positive electrical potential of +80 mV maintained within the scala media by the stria vascularis is known as the [___].
back:
* Endocochlear potential.
* Created by high K+ concentration.
* Sensitizes hair cells to sound vibrations.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient develops permanent hearing loss after a course of high-dose Gentamicin. Describe the cellular pathology underlying this drug-induced deafness.
back:
* Destruction of hair cells.
* Occurs in the Organ of Corti.
* Receptors cannot regenerate; causes sensorineural loss.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Describe the mechanical transformation that occurs within the Organ of Corti when the basilar membrane moves upward toward the scala media.
back:
* Reticular lamina rocks upward/inward.
* Stereocilia shear against tectorial membrane.
* Mechanical bending opens K+ channels.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish between the ionic composition of perilymph and endolymph within the cochlear chambers.
back:
* Perilymph: High Na+, Low K+ (CSF-like).
* Endolymph: High K+, Low Na+ (Intracellular-like).
* Endolymph is found in the scala media.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the structure that acts as a 'pressure relief valve' by bulging outward into the middle ear as the stapes faceplate moves inward.
back:
* Round window.
* Essential for fluid movement in the cochlea.
* Without it, fluid cannot vibrate due to incompressibility.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
coreConcept: Receptor Cells of the Organ of Corti
front: The specialized sensory receptors within the organ of Corti that generate nerve impulses in response to sound vibrations are the [___].
back:
● Hair cells (Inner and Outer).
● Inner hair cells: Primary transducers of sound.
● Outer hair cells: Enhance sensitivity (cochlear amplifier).
● Stereocilia: Projections that bend to open ion channels.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A patient treated with high-dose Gentamicin for a severe infection develops permanent sensorineural hearing loss. This occurs because aminoglycosides are specifically toxic to the [___].
back:
● Organ of Corti (Hair cells).
● Primary damage occurs in outer hair cells and stereocilia.
● Leads to irreversible destruction of receptor cells.
● Typically results in high-frequency hearing loss initially.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Explain the distinct functional roles of inner hair cells compared to outer hair cells in the transduction of sound.
back:
● Inner hair cells (90-95% of afferents): Main transducers of sound signals to the auditory nerve.
● Outer hair cells: Act as 'tuners' or cochlear amplifiers.
● Mechanism: Outer hair cells change length (electromotility) to adjust sensitivity to different pitches.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
coreConcept: Shearing Mechanism of the Organ of Corti
front: Contrast the mechanical movement of the hair cell stereocilia against the tectorial membrane during basilar membrane vibration.
back:
● Basilar membrane: Vibrates vertically with sound waves.
● Tectorial membrane: Stationary or moves horizontally relative to hairs.
● Shearing Action: Differential movement causes stereocilia to bend horizontally.
● Effect: Triggers the mechanical opening of potassium channels.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Identify the ion primarily responsible for depolarizing hair cells upon the bending of stereocilia toward the longest cilium.
back:
● Potassium (K+).
● Source: Enters from high-K+ endolymph of the scala media.
● Mechanism: Tip links pull open mechanosensitive cation channels.
● Result: Rapid influx down a steep 150 mV electrochemical gradient.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: The rigid structure composed of triangular rods of Corti that supports the apical ends of hair cells and moves as a unit with the basilar fibers is the [___].
back:
● Reticular lamina.
● Function: Holds the 'tops' of hair cells in a rigid frame.
● Importance: Ensures efficient shearing of stereocilia against the tectorial membrane.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A researcher observes that blocking the metabolic activity of the stria vascularis leads to immediate loss of hearing sensitivity. This occurs due to the disappearance of the [___].
back:
● Endocochlear Potential (+80 mV).
● Origin: Secreted by stria vascularis into the endolymph.
● Significance: Increases electrical potential at the stereocilia tips to 150 mV.
● Result: Dramatically increases sensitivity to weak sounds.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Describe the mechanical role of 'tip links' in the activation of the organ of Corti's hair cells.
back:
● Anatomy: Thin protein filaments connecting shorter stereocilia to adjacent longer ones.
● Trigger: Bending toward the longer hairs tugs the filaments.
● Transduction: Directly pulls open 200–300 cation channels per hair cell.
● Result: Instantaneous depolarization via K+ influx.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Contrast the chemical environment bathing the apical stereocilia with that bathing the basal portion of a hair cell.
back:
● Apical (Stereocilia): Bathed in endolymph (High K+, Low Na+).
● Basal (Body): Bathed in perilymph (High Na+, Low K+).
● Potentials: Endolymph is +80 mV; Perilymph is 0 mV.
● Purpose: Creates high drive for K+ to enter the cell upon channel opening.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Name the group of bipolar neurons located in the modiolus that receive signals from hair cells to form the cochlear nerve.
back:
● Spiral ganglion (of Corti).
● Count: Approximately 30,000 neurons in humans.
● Afferents: Over 90% specifically innervate inner hair cells.
● Axons: Exit the cochlea to become the auditory branch of CN VIII.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The short, stiff fibers of the basilar membrane near the base resonate with high frequencies, while the long, limber fibers near the [___] vibrate best at low frequencies.
back:
• Helicotrema (cochlear apex).
• Fiber length increases 12-fold from base to apex.
• Overall fiber stiffness decreases 100-fold toward the apex to allow low-frequency resonance.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: An elderly patient presents with selective hearing loss for high-pitched sounds (Presbycusis). Based on the 'place principle,' pathological changes are most likely located at which specific region of the cochlea?
back:
• Base of the cochlea (near oval window).
• High-frequency waves reach resonance and dissipate energy early at the base.
• These short, stiff fibers are most vulnerable to age-related damage.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain the mechanical sequence that initiates a 'traveling wave' along the basilar membrane following stapes movement.
back:
• Stapes moves inward at the oval window.
• Fluid pressure bends the basilar membrane toward the round window.
• Elastic tension in the fibers initiates a wave moving from base to helicotrema.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Inner vs. Outer Hair Cell Function
front: Contrast the primary physiological roles of inner hair cells versus outer hair cells during sound transduction.
back:
• Inner: Primary transducers; stimulate 90-95% of auditory nerve fibers.
• Outer: 'Tuning' mechanism; adjust sensitivity of inner cells via electromotility.
• Damage to outer cells causes deafness despite intact inner cells.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Identify the specific ion and its direction of movement responsible for the initial depolarization of a hair cell's receptor potential.
back:
• Influx of Potassium (K+) ions.
• Mechanical opening of cation channels at stereocilia tips.
• K+ moves from high-concentration endolymph (+80mV) into the hair cell (-70mV).

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: The [___] potential, measuring approximately +80 mV, is generated by the stria vascularis and is essential for sensitizing hair cells to weak sounds.
back:
• Endocochlear potential.
• Maintained by secretion of K+ into the scala media.
• Creates a +150 mV gradient between endolymph and the hair cell interior.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: A patient with damage to the apical half of the cochlea can still discriminate sound frequencies below 200 Hz. Identify the physiological principle that allows this.
back:
• Volley (Frequency) Principle.
• Nerve impulses fire in synchrony with sound wave frequency.
• Used by the brain for low-frequency discrimination (20–2000 Hz) when the place principle is insufficient.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
coreConcept: Shearing Action in Organ of Corti
front: How does the structural movement of the 'reticular lamina' contribute to the excitation of hair cells within the Organ of Corti?
back:
• Reticular lamina moves as a rigid unit with basilar fibers.
• Upward/inward rocking causes stereocilia to shear against the stationary tectorial membrane.
• This shearing force mechanically opens ion channels at stereocilia tips.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Distinguish between the fluid compartments of the cochlea regarding their ionic composition and anatomical location.
back:
• Perilymph (Scala Vestibuli/Tympani): High Na+, low K+; similar to CSF.
• Endolymph (Scala Media): High K+, low Na+; unique positive potential (+80mV).
• Separated by Reissner's and Basilar membranes.

category: Describe the mechanism of transmission of sound waves in cochlea
front: Explain why Reissner’s membrane does not significantly impede the transmission of sound vibrations from the scala vestibuli to the scala media.
back:
• It is extremely thin and easily moved.
• Offers negligible resistance to fluid vibrations.
• Scala vestibuli and scala media act as a single chamber for sound conduction.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: The primary sensory receptors responsible for transmitting approximately 90% to 95% of auditory signals to the brain are the [___].
back:
• Inner hair cells
• Only 3,500 in number (compared to 12,000 outer cells)
• Essential for actual sound detection and frequency discrimination.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A patient is found to have intact inner hair cells but selective destruction of the outer hair cells. Predict the primary physiological consequence on hearing.
back:
• Significant hearing loss (sensitivity decrease)
• Loss of "tuning" capability
• Difficulty discriminating between specific sound pitches/frequencies.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Explain the mechanical event at the stereocilia that leads to hair cell depolarization upon basilar membrane vibration.
back:
• Stereocilia bend toward the longest cilium
• Tip links tug on and open cation channels
• Potassium (K+) influx from endolymph occurs
• Cell membrane potential becomes less negative.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Contrast the ionic composition and electrical potential of endolymph within the scala media with the surrounding perilymph.
back:
• Endolymph: High K+, Low Na+; +80mV potential
• Perilymph: High Na+, Low K+; 0mV potential
• Gradient: Creates a 150mV electrical potential at stereocilia tips.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Identify the specific role of the stria vascularis in maintaining the electrical environment of the organ of Corti.
back:
• Secretes endolymph
• Maintains high potassium (K+) concentration
• Generates the +80mV endocochlear potential essential for hair cell sensitivity.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: The rapid-acting excitatory neurotransmitter released by the base of hair cells into the synapse of the cochlear nerve is [___].
back:
• Glutamate
• Released upon opening of voltage-gated Calcium channels
• Triggers action potentials in the spiral ganglion neurons.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A researcher observes that a rigid structure composed of the rods of Corti and a flat plate fails to move as a unit. Identify the affected structure and the likely impact on hearing.
back:
• Reticular lamina
• Prevents shearing of hairs against the tectorial membrane
• Results in failure of mechanical-to-electrical transduction.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: How does the organ of Corti achieve repolarization following the termination of a sound vibration?
back:
• Closure of apical cation channels (mechanical)
• Exit of K+ through calcium-sensitive potassium channels at the cell base
• Efflux into the surrounding perilymph.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Distinguish between the primary mechanical function of the basilar membrane and the tectorial membrane in sound perception.
back:
• Basilar Membrane: Vibrates in response to fluid waves; supports organ of Corti
• Tectorial Membrane: Stationary gel; stereocilia shear against it to open channels.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Locate the primary neuronal cell bodies whose axons form the cochlear nerve and receive signals from the hair cells.
back:
• Spiral Ganglion of Corti
• Situated in the modiolus (central bony core)
• Approximately 30,000 neurons per cochlea.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: The primary receptor organ located on the surface of the basilar membrane that generates nerve impulses in response to sound vibrations is the [___].
back:
* Organ of Corti
* Contains sensory hair cells (inner and outer).
* Rests on the fibrous basilar membrane.
* Covered by the gelatinous tectorial membrane.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A patient is diagnosed with selective damage to the 12,000 cells in the organ of Corti responsible for 'tuning' the ear's sensitivity. Identify these cells and their primary function.
back:
* Outer Hair Cells
* Adjust sensitivity of inner hair cells at various pitches.
* Controlled by retrograde nerve fibers from the brainstem.
* Damage causes significant loss of hearing sensitivity despite intact inner hair cells.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Explain the ionic mechanism of depolarization within the stereocilia of the organ of Corti upon mechanical stimulation.
back:
* Mechanical bending opens tip-link gated cation channels.
* Potassium (K+) flows from high-concentration endolymph into the hair cell.
* Resulting depolarization opens voltage-gated calcium channels.
* Triggers release of glutamate to stimulate cochlear nerve endings.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Contrast the chemical composition and electrical status of the Endolymph found in the scala media with the Perilymph of the scala vestibuli.
back:
* Endolymph: High K+, Low Na+; +80 mV potential (endocochlear potential).
* Perilymph: High Na+, Low K+; 0 mV potential (similar to CSF).
* Interaction: Creates a 150 mV gradient at the hair cell tips to maximize sensitivity.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Describe the 'shearing' mechanism between the tectorial membrane and the hair cells during basilar membrane vibration.
back:
* Basilar membrane movement rocks the reticular lamina upward and inward.
* The tectorial membrane remains relatively stationary.
* This creates a shearing force that bends stereocilia against the tectorial gel.
* Translates mechanical fluid waves into receptor potentials.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
coreConcept: Anatomical Location of the Organ of Corti
front: The sensory receptor organ for hearing, known as the organ of Corti, is located on the surface of the [___] within the cochlea.
back:
• Basilar membrane.
• It separates the scala media from the scala tympani.
• Vibrates in response to fluid waves in the cochlea.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: A patient with aminoglycoside toxicity presents with significant hearing loss. Histology reveals damage to the three rows of hair cells responsible for tuning pitch sensitivity rather than direct signal transmission. These are the [___] hair cells.
back:
• Outer Hair Cells.
• Number approximately 12,000.
• Receive retrograde inhibitory signals from the brainstem to 'tune' pitch sensitivity.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Describe the ionic mechanism of hair cell depolarization within the organ of Corti when stereocilia are bent toward the kinocilium (longer cilium).
back:
• Tip links open mechanical cation channels.
• K+ ions influx from high-potassium endolymph.
• Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open, triggering glutamate release.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
front: Contrast the numerical distribution and functional importance of inner hair cells versus outer hair cells in the auditory system.
back:
• Inner: Single row (~3,500); transmit 90-95% of auditory nerve signals.
• Outer: 3-4 rows (~12,000); primarily modulate/tune receptor sensitivity.
• Damage to outer cells causes massive hearing loss despite fewer nerve connections.

category: Describe the physiological anatomy and function of organ of Corti
